title: Sequential Fair Allocation With Replenishments: A Little Envy Goes An Exponentially Long Way: the policy-constants lemma (finite expected hitting times and boundary hit probabilities)
author: Chido Onyeze, Sean R. Sinclair, Chamsi Hssaine, Siddhartha Banerjee
work: Sequential Fair Allocation With Replenishments: A Little Envy Goes An Exponentially Long Way
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the policy-constants lemma of "Sequential Fair Allocation With Replenishments", printed as Lemma 3 of the arXiv version (source0.tex lines 1413--1426, label lem:policy_constants, restatable name PolicyBounds), delivered together with the paper's own complete proof of it at source0.tex lines 1427--1491 (65 lines, a single adjacent proof environment). The lemma is the paper's hypothesis-checking result: it gives sufficient conditions on the supply and demand distributions under which the expected hitting times E(M), E(0), the boundary hit probabilities p_M, p_0 and the expected positive and negative parts of the drift are all finite and non-degenerate, and the paper invokes it in exactly that role ("the conditions of Lemma 3 (see Appendix B.1) hold, and H_M and H_0 exist") before every one of its achievability theorems. The proof is complete and closed inside the retained span. Part (i): with L = ceil(M/epsilon) and the assumption Pr(Z_t(alpha) <= -epsilon) >= delta, the tail-sum formula gives E[tau_0(S)] <= L * sum_{k>=0} Pr(tau_0(S) > kL); the increment of Pr(tau_0(S) <= kL) is conditioned on the event E^-_L = {Z_1 <= -epsilon, ..., Z_L <= -epsilon}, whose probability is at least delta^L by independence of (B_t, N_t) across time; on E^-_L the unreflected process Q_t falls by at least L*epsilon >= M, so the process must have hit 0 by round kL independently of where it started at round (k-1)L, giving Pr(tau_0(S) > kL) <= (1-delta^L)^k and hence E[tau_0(S)] <= L/delta^L < infinity; the mirror argument with E^+_L gives E[tau_M(S)] < infinity. Part (ii) is the immediate almost-sure consequence of finiteness of the expectations. Part (iii): a one-step return to M happens whenever Z_1 >= epsilon, so p_M >= Pr(Z_1 >= epsilon | S_0 = M) >= delta > 0, while on E^-_L the process hits 0 within the first L rounds before it can return to M, so Pr(S_{tau(M)} = 0 | S_0 = M) >= delta^L and p_M <= 1 - delta^L < 1; the case of p_0 is the symmetric one, and the proof says so. Part (iv) is the layer-cake bound E[Z(alpha)^+] >= epsilon * Pr(Z(alpha) >= epsilon) >= epsilon*delta, with the mirror for the negative part. All four enumerated claims are proved, the constants are explicit in epsilon and delta, and nothing is deferred to another part of the paper. The argument is a genuine finite-hitting-time/geometric-trials computation (tail-sum formula, conditioning on a run of L unfavourable increments, geometric domination, one-step recurrence and transience), not a restatement of a textbook fact, and it is the necessary technical step for the paper's exponential inefficiency bounds; it does not, however, use the paper's heavier optional-stopping and martingale machinery, which is where the paper's H3-level content sits, so the unit is rated H2. The chosen unit is a lemma rather than the paper's headline theorem by necessity: the headline expression theorem is printed in the main body (source0.tex lines 639--646) while its full proof sits detached in Appendix C (lines 1496--1533) and depends on the paper's renewal-cycle figure and a textbook citation, and the only other adjacent complete proofs in the paper are two short propositions (lines 1312--1344 and 1838--1856); the counted lemma is the strongest statement in the paper whose own complete proof is adjacent to it and whose dependencies are all retained here.
